content.text:
I identify DyRhO3 (mp-1212884) as the only phase present.

1. **Three strongest peaks.** The observed pattern has a strong single peak at about 32.5°, with partner peaks at about 30.5° and 33.7°. In the simulated DyRhO3 pattern these are its three main reflections: (020), (112) and (200), simulated at about 30.7°, 32.7° and 33.9°. The observed intensities are roughly 20, 100 and 25, against simulated values of about 17, 100 and 23. The whole observed set sits about 0.2° lower, which fits a slightly larger unit cell.
2. **Weaker peaks.** The observed peaks at about 25.4° and 39° also line up with DyRhO3 reflections.
3. **Closest alternative.** Sm2MnNiO6 has a similar perovskite-type cell. It would put a peak near 31.7°, where the observed pattern is flat, and its other peaks are in the wrong places.
4. **Other candidates.** Na3EuTi2Nb2O12 would give a clear peak at 22.6° (about 27% of its strongest), and the observed pattern shows only noise there. PtO2's strongest peak would sit near 27.4°, where nothing is seen either. I simulated only the first three candidates; the borates and the remaining phases were not checked peak by peak.
5. **Second phase.** I see no unexplained peak above the noise, which runs to about 10 units, so I report one phase.
